answer: Because the kernel index resolves every citation against the marble checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the garden audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 22 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
